name: WeldForge
description: Multi-tenant federated identity platform: SSO (OIDC, SAML 2.0), CIAM, SCIM 2.0 provisioning, MFA (TOTP/WebAuthn/SMS), internal per-tenant PKI (CA/CRL/OCSP), M2M auth (scoped API keys, service-account tokens, OAuth 2.0 client credentials), HMAC-signed audit webhooks.
openApiAccess: Not routed on the public host. /v3/api-docs and /swagger-ui/index.html return the portal's HTML, not a spec, because the ingress forwards only /api, /t/, /saml2, /scim and /health to the backend. Run the container yourself (docker compose up) and read them at http://localhost:8076. Build integrations from /llms.txt and /agents.html, not from a fetched spec.

tokenFormats.notes: Returned once in response body as 'apiKey'. Stored hashed (SHA-256) server-side; plaintext is never retrievable.
Returned once in response body as 'token'. Unlike app-client keys, these carry admin authorisation in SecurityContext — use for agents that must call admin endpoints.

crossTenantAdmin.purpose: An admin whose token carries SUPER_ADMIN / a global admin membership targets a tenant other than their own by adding 'X-WF-Tenant: <slug>'. The effective admin role is re-resolved against that tenant, the call is audited, and a caller with no reach into the target is rejected 403.

endUserAuthForms.purpose: User-facing auth screens -- where humans land in a browser to sign in, reset a password, register, or verify an email. Served both from the apex host https://sso.weldforge.org and from each tenant's own subdomain, so password managers (Chrome/Firefox/Safari/Bitwarden/1Password) treat each tenant as a distinct site.
endUserAuthForms.hostPattern: https://{slug}.sso.weldforge.org (live; wildcard DNS and TLS are provisioned)
endUserAuthForms.removedLegacyForm: Old URLs of the form https://sso.weldforge.org/{path}?tenant={slug} have been removed. Do not generate them.
endUserAuthForms.cookieScoping: Session cookies (wf_session, refresh_token) are set without a Domain attribute, so they are scoped to the exact subdomain. A session on acme.sso.weldforge.org does not authenticate against contoso.sso.weldforge.org.
endUserAuthForms.apexHostPattern: https://sso.weldforge.org (live; use when the tenant slug is unknown)
endUserAuthForms.slugRules: Leftmost host label. Must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}[a-z0-9]$ and may not be one of the reserved root labels: www, api, admin, app, mail, static.
endUserAuthForms.tenantResolution: A tenant subdomain sets the tenant implicitly, so requests to it need no X-Tenant-Slug header. On the apex host the header is required, or the request resolves to the 'default' tenant and succeeds in the wrong place.
endUserAuthForms.indexing: Every response from this host carries X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow. Do not index or crawl the auth forms.

endUserAuthentication.logout: POST /api/auth/logout-all (revokes every refresh token for the user; there is no per-session /api/auth/logout - a browser session ends by clearing the cookie, and OIDC RPs use GET /t/{slug}/oauth2/logout)
endUserAuthentication.signUpTenantHeader: X-Tenant-Slug selects the tenant on POST /api/auth/register; without it the request resolves to the 'default' tenant
endUserAuthentication.signUpApiKey: none - /api/auth/** is exempt from x-app-authorization, because a browser calls it before the user has credentials

signUpErrors.400 bad_request: email already used in this tenant
signUpErrors.409 seat_limit_exceeded: tenant at maxUsers; body carries limit and current
signUpErrors.429 too_many_requests: rate limited; retryAfterSeconds says how long

keyAdminEndpoints.purpose: Invite a user — creates the user in an invited state and returns a 7-day reset token
Register a SAML SP the IdP will assert to
Wire a CRM push target (Salesforce, HubSpot, Dynamics, Pipedrive)
Bootstrap a root CA for the tenant
Bind a SCIM group to an admin role

shape.error: string — machine-readable code (e.g. not_found, bad_request, unauthorized, forbidden, validation_error, provider_unavailable, internal_error)
shape.message: string — human-readable detail (never leaks a stack trace)

observability.health: GET /health (public, JSON) -- the only externally reachable health endpoint.
observability.actuatorNote: /actuator/** is NOT routed by the public ingress; a request falls through to the SPA and returns HTML. The paths below exist inside the cluster only and are scraped in-cluster by Prometheus. Do not poll them from outside.

rateLimits.strategy: per-identity (API key or service account), sliding window
rateLimits.notes: Specific limits per endpoint are enforced but not published; expect 429 with Retry-After on overrun.

adminPortalNote: The admin SPA is served from the same host as the API; the ingress routes /api, /t/, /saml2, /scim and /health to the backend and everything else to the portal. admin.weldforge.org does not resolve -- do not use it.

hostedSignup.purpose: Subscribe to the hosted platform. This creates a tenant; it is not the same as registering a user inside an existing tenant (see endUserAuthForms).
hostedSignup.authentication: None. Browser-facing, like /api/auth/**. Do not send x-app-authorization.
hostedSignup.requestBody: {tier, organisation, contactName, contactEmail, tenantSlug, region, billingCycle, currency, billingCountry, termsAccepted}

nextStep.CHECKOUT: checkoutUrl is set; send the customer there to pay. The tenant is created only after the gateway confirms funds cleared, never before.
nextStep.MANUAL_FOLLOW_UP: checkoutUrl is null. The order is recorded and the slug reserved, but no payment gateway is configured for that currency/country, so a human completes it.

hostedSignup.criticalNote: Branch on nextStep, never on whether checkoutUrl is present. A null checkoutUrl is not an error and must not be retried -- the sign-up has been accepted either way.
hostedSignup.slugReservation: The requested slug is validated with the same rules as the admin path and held while the order is live. A 400 naming the slug means choose another.
hostedSignup.selfHostAlternative: Self-hosting needs none of this. The source is complete and 'docker compose up' is the whole quick start: https://github.com/weldforge-idp/weldforge

mfa.challenge: POST /api/auth/login answers {mfaRequired: true, mfaChallengeToken: '<JWT>'} instead of a session. This is not a failure.
mfa.tokenShape: The challenge token is a JWT, several hundred characters. Do not assume a short opaque string and do not use it as a database key.
mfa.redeem: POST /api/auth/mfa/verify with {challengeToken, type, code, backupCode, webauthnResponse} -- the challenge token plus exactly one of the last three.

factors.WEBAUTHN: Passkeys, Windows Hello, Touch ID, security keys. First POST /api/auth/mfa/webauthn/assertion/start with {challengeToken}; it answers {publicKey: '<options JSON>'}. Run the browser ceremony and send the serialised result as webauthnResponse. There is no .../assertion/finish endpoint.
factors.BACKUP_CODE: One-time recovery code in 'backupCode'. Issued when the user enrols their first factor; each works once. This path is taken whenever backupCode is non-blank, regardless of 'type'.

responses.429: Account locked. Failed factor attempts feed the same lockout counter as failed passwords, so retrying in a loop locks the account.

relyingPartyOnboarding.purpose: Register an application as an OIDC relying party in a tenant, and obtain the three values the app needs: issuer, client id, client secret.
relyingPartyOnboarding.authentication: x-app-authorization: wf_svc_* (SUPER_ADMIN, or TENANT_ADMIN on the target tenant). A user bearer JWT is also accepted.

actingInAnotherTenant.note: There is NO token-exchange step. A SUPER_ADMIN does not mint a tenant-scoped token to act in another tenant; it names the tenant in this header. Membership-checked, audited, and refused (403/404) rather than falling back to the caller's own tenant.
actingInAnotherTenant.legacyAlias: X-Tenant-Slug is accepted after authentication, but means something different before it. Prefer X-WF-Tenant.

requestBody.clientId: string, optional - generated as wf_client_<uuid> if omitted
requestBody.name: string
requestBody.webOrigins: array, optional - drives CORS on the tenant OIDC endpoints; browser apps only
requestBody.requirePkce: boolean, optional - defaults TRUE. See clientTypes below.
requestBody.tokenEndpointAuthMethod: string, optional - "none" makes the client public

clientTypes.confidentialWithPkce: Default when requirePkce is omitted. A client secret IS issued and PKCE is enforced - they are not alternatives. Correct for server-side web apps (Auth.js/NextAuth, Django, Rails).
clientTypes.public: tokenEndpointAuthMethod:"none" or publicClient:true. PKCE-only, no secret is ever surfaced. Correct for browser SPAs and native apps (RFC 8252).
clientTypes.pkceDisabled: requirePkce:false. Supported but rarely needed: libraries that send a client secret also send PKCE when discovery advertises S256, which it does. Request only if the client library cannot do PKCE at all.

relyingPartyOnboarding.secretSemantics: clientSecret is returned ONLY in the create response and in POST /api/admin/oidc/clients/{id}/rotate-secret. GET never returns it. If lost it cannot be read back - rotate, which invalidates the old secret.

returnsToTheApplication.clientSecret: clientSecret from the create response (shown once)

relyingPartyOnboarding.scopeNotes: scopes_supported advertises openid, profile, email. The standard scopes address, phone and offline_access are accepted but not advertised. Refresh tokens follow from grantTypes containing refresh_token, NOT from offline_access.
relyingPartyOnboarding.claimNotes: Claims follow granted scopes (OIDC Core 5.4): sub always, email with the email scope, name/picture with profile. email_verified is emitted as a standard claim - treat an ABSENT value as unknown, not false, since tokens minted before the claim existed do not carry it.
relyingPartyOnboarding.tenantSlugRules: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}[a-z0-9]$, not a reserved root label (www, api, admin, app, ...), and checked against a holdback list. A slug becomes a live subdomain.

dynamicClientRegistration.status: Returns 403 on every call as of 2026-09-20. The endpoint routes publicly but delegates to an admin-scoped service, so an anonymous RFC 7591 registration - the only kind - is refused. Known defect. Use the admin endpoint above; do not build a flow on this until this note changes.
